small_guidance: The BN fusion uses var computed over dims=(0,2,3,4) but applies a per-channel mean subtraction over only spatial dims — this changes the output because the reference subtracts the per-(N,C) spatial mean *after* BN (which uses running_mean/running_var in eval, but the harness runs in training mode where BN normalizes by batch stats). Recompute scale using BN training-mode stats: mean over (0,2,3,4) and var over (0,2,3,4), then y_bn = (y - mean_bc) * gamma/sqrt(var+eps) + beta, then subtract per-(N,C) spatial mean. Pass beta and per-channel batch-mean into the fused kernel and do (x - bn_mean[c]) * scale[c] + beta[c], then subtract the spatial mean of that result in a second pass within the same kernel. Also update BN running stats to match training-mode side effects.
large_guidance: Redesign the tail as a single fused kernel that, for each (N,C) row: (1) loads y, (2) computes spatial sum to get per-(N,C) spatial mean of the *post-BN* tensor analytically as scale*(spatial_mean(y) - bn_mean) + beta, (3) emits scale*(y - bn_mean) + beta - post_bn_spatial_mean = scale*(y - spatial_mean_y). Note this simplification means the final output reduces to gamma/sqrt(var_bc+eps) * (y - spatial_mean_bc(y)); beta cancels. So the correct fused kernel only needs per-channel batch var (computed across N and spatial in a separate reduction kernel matching training-mode BN) and per-(N,C) spatial mean of y. Keep the ConvTranspose3d gemm kernel as-is; rebuild only the epilogue with this algebra and verify against reference under training=True.
